Notes: Andersen's adhi entry compares RV ádhi and Pali adhi; Turner 249 lists those forms with the sense 'up, above, on'. The attested preposition is the inherited item, not the distinct derivative ádhika. Andersen 1990 Ashokan image-checked glossary heads and source variant

Andersen calls aṁta plural 'borderers; neighbors' and compares RV ánta, Pali anta. Turner 347 has the boundary/proximity noun and Prakrit aṁta; the human plural reflects a straightforward boundary-dweller sense, though Turner does not list this precise Ashokan use. Andersen 1990 Ashokan image-checked glossary heads and source variant

Andersen lists aṁtala 'time interval' beside RV ántara and Pali antara, separating -r- Gu from -l- Bh/Ah/Sa. Turner 357 explicitly gives Ashokan kāl./dh./jau. aṁtala and 'long period' aṁtara under its first ántara section. Andersen 1990 Ashokan image-checked glossary heads and source variant

Andersen compares RV ēvá and Pali eva/va for 'so, just, even'. Turner 2524 explicitly lists Ashokan eva, yeva and man. vaṁ as continuations of the emphatic particle. Andersen 1990 Ashokan image-checked glossary heads and source variant

The printed glossary gives RV ná, Pali na for the negative particle. Turner 6906 explicitly lists Ashokan na, with kāl. nā, for this exact function. Andersen 1990 Ashokan image-checked glossary heads and source variant

Andersen gives RV padá and Pali pada for 'quarter; foot, path, place'. Turner 7747 groups the footstep, track and place senses with Pali pada; this is the first padá branch, not *pada 'tendon'. Andersen 1990 Ashokan image-checked glossary heads and source variant

Andersen prints paṁnā 'fifty' and compares RV pañcāśát with Pali paññāsa/paṇṇāsa. Turner 7682 gives the same Pali assimilated numeral and the Prakrit paṇṇā forms. Andersen 1990 Ashokan image-checked glossary heads and source variant

Andersen prints pavata 'mountain, rock' beside RV párvata and Pali pabbata. Turner 7945 explicitly cites Ashokan pavatasi and the rock/mountain sense; 7945-2 is a later -ll- extension and 7946 is a fish. Andersen 1990 Ashokan image-checked glossary heads and source variant

Andersen's pitu 'father' compares RV pitr̥ and Pali pitar, noting the Brahmagiri piti- variant. Turner 8179 lists pitúḥ in the Old Indo-Aryan paradigm and Ashokan pituna, the same stem's inflection. Andersen 1990 Ashokan image-checked glossary heads and source variant

The glossary has rāja 'king' with RV rā́jan and Pali rāja; the printed -ā citation is nominative. Turner 10679 explicitly lists Ashokan gir. rājā/rāño and other Ashokan regional forms under rā́jan. Andersen 1990 Ashokan image-checked glossary heads and source variant

Andersen prints vaṁṇa 'colour' and compares RV várṇa, Pali vaṇṇa. Turner 11338 is the appearance/colour/class branch and has Pali vaṇṇa; 11339 is the separate 'sound, syllable' branch. Andersen 1990 Ashokan image-checked glossary heads and source variant

Andersen distinguishes vasa 'year' from vas 'live', gives RV varṣá/Pali vassa, and says this Ashokan use is plural. Turner 11392 section 2 specifically lists Ashokan kāl./dh./jau. vasa 'year'; the rain branch is not the intended sense. Andersen 1990 Ashokan image-checked glossary heads and source variant

Andersen gives hevam 'so, thus' beside RV ēvám and Pali evaṁ. Turner 2527 explicitly includes Ashokan evaṁ and he- forms; this is the adverb, not emphatic ēvá 2524. Andersen 1990 Ashokan image-checked glossary heads and source variant

Andersen's separate sāvaṇa line on printed p. 174 explicitly says 'see sāvana-'. The target is the already saved source head for 'announcement, edict' (CDIAL 12698), not the month-name śrāvaṇa 12699. The source record's blank gloss is preserved. Andersen 1990 Ashokan image-checked glossary heads and source variant
